## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Top call is justified and probability is calibrated. Four independent doses (0.1–3.0 µM, dose indices 4–7, one well per dose but multiple fields per well; each effect present across all doses) show overwhelming hyper-intense tubulin with high contrast, e.g. tub_mean z ≈39–46 and stronger tub_std/tubulin contrast features (about z ≈63–80 for tub_std), consistent with stabilized microtubule bundles rather than loss seen for destabilizers. Direct phenotype description confirms thick perinuclear tubulin bundles/coils/rings versus diffuse vehicle filaments and rounded condensed-DNA cells. Epithelial screening atlas comparison is unanimous: 4/4 wells map to Microtubule stabilizers with similarities ≈0.83–0.86, nearest competing classes only ≈0.51. Actin brightening is plausibly secondary to rounding/retraction and does not rescue Eg5/destabilizer or Actin-disruptor alternatives, which would not generate interphase bundled tubulin of this magnitude. Dose–response flatness reflects saturation already by 0.1 µM, not a weak effect; a lower-dose onset point (dose index 3, replicate 1) would be informative but cannot change the decisive classification and no budget remains. The uniform saturated high-similarity profile across all active high doses and absence of any contrary signal (each well independently converges on the same atlas class) make a replicate/quieter-dose well unnecessary to resolve stabilizer vs destabilizer vs Eg5 decisively; an added well might refine the EC50 but cannot credibly overturn the unanimous NSC conclusion or recalibrate the stated probability.

## Unblinding

Compound: **taxol** (PubChem CID [36314](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/36314))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: Tubulin inhibitor

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: the call was **Microtubule stabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Microtubule stabilizers**.

The final call is the nearest-neighbour vote over the 4 wells the agent chose (4/4). The Scientist's own call was **Microtubule stabilizers** (agrees; right).

## Reflection

The call was driven by extreme, saturated tubulin signals from the first two wells (tub_std z +74.7 to +75.1, tub_glcm_contrast z +59 to +65 at 0.3 and 3 uM) and a unanimous atlas vote for Microtubule stabilizers, later extended to 4/4 wells with similarities 0.826-0.86 (PMID 25213191; PMID 31029218). Visual description of thick perinuclear bundles/coils/rings versus diffuse vehicle filaments plus rounded condensed-DNA cells correctly resolved the stabilizer versus destabilizer alternative that intensity alone could leave ambiguous.

The dose_response check was misleading if read naively: tub_mean rho +0.20 p=0.8 over 0.1-3 uM suggested no dose dependence, but this reflected saturation already by 0.1 uM, not a weak effect. That was an acquisition choice failure — starting mid-high and staying high (doses 4-7 only) missed the onset, so no EC50 could be estimated and the flat curve added nothing.

Minor competing k-neighbour votes for Microtubule destabilizers (2/10) and Eg5 inhibitors (2/10) did not overturn the NSC majority, and actin brightening was correctly treated as secondary rounding rather than an actin mechanism. The second literature search was too narrow and returned 0 hits, adding no phenotypic support.

What was right:
- Acquiring mid-high wells first (0.3 and 3 uM) immediately revealed overwhelming hyper-intense, high-contrast tubulin (tub_std z ~75, tub_mean z ~43-46) consistent with bundles, not destabilizer loss
- Atlas comparison giving unanimous 4/4 NSC votes for Microtubule stabilizers with similarities 0.826-0.86 versus ~0.51 for competitors correctly excluded destabilizers and Eg5 inhibitors
- Microscopist description of thick perinuclear bundles/coils/rings versus diffuse DMSO filaments plus lower density/rounded cells provided direct visual confirmation of stabilizer phenotype

What was wrong or missed:
- Dose-response over only saturated wells (0.1-3 uM) gave rho +0.20 p=0.8, which looked like lack of dose dependence until recognized as saturation
- Acquisition plan sampled only doses 4-7 and never sampled low doses (0.001-0.03 uM), missing the onset/EC50 that would have strengthened dose-dependence evidence
- Second literature query on bundling/mitotic arrest phenotype was too specific and returned 0 hits, contributing nothing to validation

Proposed next experiment: Low-dose titration (0.001-0.1 uM) with fixed high-resolution tubulin immunofluorescence plus phospho-histone H3 to define onset EC50 and directly distinguish stabilized interphase bundles from Eg5-inhibitor monopolar spindles.
